findings.body: The doc comment promises "Shorten `text` to at most `limit` characters". When `head` contains no space, the `None` branch returns `head` (exactly `limit` chars) plus the ellipsis char, i.e. `limit + 1` characters. For a concrete reachable input such as `shorten("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz", 20)` the result is 21 characters. A caller that passes a hard ceiling as `limit` (the documented use is check-run titles capped by GitHub) would exceed that ceiling by one on any single-token / no-space title, triggering GitHub's own truncation or rejection. The `Some` branch is already within `limit` because `space < limit`; only the `None` branch overshoots. Fix by reserving one character of head for the ellipsis when there is no word boundary to break on.
findings.title: Keep shorten output within the documented limit on spaceless input

value.summary: The module adds `shorten` and `first_sentence` helpers with multibyte-safe slicing and tests. `shorten` violates its own documented contract: the no-space branch emits `limit + 1` characters rather than at most `limit`, which matters when `limit` is a hard cap (e.g. a GitHub check-run title ceiling).
